title: Caselet Business Analytics DI
tagline: Year 4 — Business situations written as paragraphs: subscribers, churn, revenue, costs and break-even from the text alone

introduction.overview: A business-analytics caselet describes a company in a paragraph and asks about revenue, profit, retention and break-even. The first step is to extract every number and what it refers to (users, a percentage of users, a price, a fixed cost, a churn rate). Then build a small model: subscribers × price = revenue; revenue − costs = profit; subscribers × (1 − churn) + additions = next month. Care with bases is essential, since each percentage refers to a particular group.
introduction.placementRelevance: Analytics caselets are common in management-oriented and IT-services aptitude tests.
introduction.realWorldContext: Product and finance teams build exactly such small models.

learningObjectives: Extract numbers and their bases from a paragraph
Project a second month with churn and additions
Avoid mixing registered users with subscribers

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Revenue = subscribers × price. Next month = this month × (1 − churn) + additions. Break-even = fixed cost ÷ contribution per unit.

coreDefinitions: Churn: share of customers lost in a period.
Contribution: price minus variable cost per unit.
Break-even: volume at which profit is zero.
Fixed cost: cost that does not change with volume.
Base: the group a percentage refers to.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A caselet is a tiny business. Write its equations and the questions answer themselves.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: List givens with their bases; compute subscribers, revenue, profit; then project the next month.

mainNarrative: A subscription app has 80,000 registered users. 5% of them are paying subscribers, each paying ₹300 per month. Fixed monthly costs (servers and support) are ₹4,00,000. Each month 8% of the existing subscribers cancel and marketing adds 400 new subscribers. Subscribers = 4,000; revenue ₹12,00,000; profit ₹8,00,000.
For the delivery firm: profit per delivery ₹10, daily ₹12,000, monthly ₹3,60,000 − ₹1,50,000 = ₹2,10,000; each rider handles 1,200 ÷ 60 = 20 orders a day.

deepDiveAspects.title: Steady state
deepDiveAspects.content: Subscribers stop changing when additions equal churn: S = 400 ÷ 0.08 = 5,000.

deepDiveAspects.title: Percent of which base
deepDiveAspects.content: Churn applies to subscribers, not registered users.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Write subscribers, revenue and profit once; project with churn and additions; use break-even for thresholds.
